section_summaries.individual_presentation: two-year history of right leg spasms and low back pain; slowly progressive stiffness of the axial muscles and proximal limb muscles, making ambulation difficult; hyperlordosis of the lumbar spine; episodic spasms precipitated by jarring or sudden movement; normal intellectual, sensory, and motor examination when not in spasm back pain severe, intermittent back spasms over the preceding week; similar but less intense low back pains and severe right leg spasms over the preceding year; history of low back pain with spasms and right lower-extremity spasms for about three years
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: diagnostic criteria for stiff-man syndrome: presence of slowly progressive stiffness of axial and proximal limb muscles; marked amelioration of symptoms with IV administration of diazepam Magnetic resonance imaging of the cervical spine three years previously had been unremarkable; MRI of the lumbosacral spine one year earlier had been inconclusive; Electromyography (EMG) performed at that time had been inconclusive Initial laboratory data showed mild anemia and serum bicarbonate of 15 mmoVL; electrolytes, WBCs, urinalysis, creatine kinase, and calcium within normal limits
section_summaries.individual_treatment: IV administration of diazepam; high-dose oral diazepam as maintenance drug treated with diazepam, 5 mg bid, and chlorzoxazone, 500 mg qid by an orthopedist given diazepam, 5 mg IV, with control of symptoms for approximately 30 minutes
section_summaries.individual_limitations: EMG and MRI results were inconclusive; severity of back spasms prevented patient from exiting car at neurologist’s office no history of psychiatric disorder; tetanus immunization was not current The patient had been seen on several prior occasions and had undergone multiple diagnostic tests before this visit without being properly diagnosed
